 Paris R1 previews and predictions: Djokovic vs. Vacherot, Paul vs. Rune 
 November 2, 2026 
 Ricky 
 Match previews 
 4 
 First-round action at the Paris Masters wraps up on Tuesday, when Novak Djokovic faces a tough opening match against Valentin Vacherot. Tommy Paul is going up against former champion Holger Rune. 
 (10) Novak Djokovic vs. Valentin Vacherot
Djokovic and Vacherot will be going head-to-head for the second time in their careers when they clash in round one of the Rolex Paris Masters on Tuesday. Their lone meeting came last fall at the Shanghai Masters, where Vacherot pulled off a shocking 6-3, 6-4 semifinal upset on his way to the title. Another victory for Vacherot would hardly be surprising, as the 27-year-old Monegasque is now an established force on the ATP Tour. Ranked 27th, he is coming off one of his best-ever results — a 500-point title in Basel on Sunday.
That being said, you have to like Djokovic’s chances in this spot. His opponent is certainly fatigued both mentally and physically, whereas Djokovic heads into Paris with plenty of rest (he lost to Jan-Lennard Struff in a third-set tiebreaker in the Basel second round). The 39-year-old’s last two events have not been great, but keep in mind that he won the Beijing title almost exactly one month ago. Although this may not be a Grand Slam version of Djokovic, it should be the next best thing in terms of motivation level. He needs a big result to qualify for the Nitto ATP Finals and is facing an opponent who beat him in their only previous matchup.
 Pick: Djokovic in 2

 (12) Tommy Paul vs. (PR) Holger Rune
Paul is also in mathematical Turin contention, but he must reach the Paris final in order to have a chance. A bad draw last week in Vienna did not help matters, as the 14th-ranked American ran into eventual champion Carlos Alcaraz in the quarterfinals and fell 6-4, 7-6(2). It was still a solid tournament for Paul, who destroyed both Andrey Rublev and Luciano Darderi in the earlier rounds.
Up first for the No. 12 seed on Tuesday is Rune, whom he surprisingly has never faced. Rune is a former Paris Masters champion (2022), but the 23-year-old Dane does not figure to be a contender this time around given that he has missed almost all of the 2026 campaign due to a torn Achilles’. His comeback has been a mixed bag so far, but his Basel efforts were encouraging. Rune won two matches in final-set tiebreakers before losing to Vacherot 6-3, 3-6, 6-3. Paul is the more battle-tested player right now and should be able to coax more than enough errors out of Rune on a fast, low-bouncing hard court.
 Pick: Paul in 3
